title: Run your channels well and find the true profit in each

say: Run your channels well, and find the true profit in each one.
This is the video for module 2: Channel Operations, Quality and True Margin.
Order-to-cash is the full path from the moment a partner orders to the moment the money is safely in your business account.

panel.heading: A sale ends when the money is recorded
items: Order-to-cash: from order to money in your account
Unclear steps mean lost orders and forgotten invoices
One short written routine for each channel

say: When any step is unclear, orders go missing, deliveries are disputed and invoices are forgotten. The sale is only finished when the money is recorded, not when the van leaves.

say: A short written routine for each channel prevents most of this. We call it an SOP, a standard operating procedure: a numbered list a helper can follow without asking you.

say: When a shop orders on WhatsApp, reply within 2 hours confirming items, quantities, price and delivery day.

panel.heading: An SOP for shop orders
items: Confirm the order within 2 hours
Log it with an order number
Pick the oldest batch first, check labels
Delivery note and invoice with due date
Count together; both sign both notes
Remind one day before payment is due

say: And keep your money safe. Take payments only into your business account, never a helper's personal account. Fake transfer alerts are a common fraud, and never share your PIN or one-time passwords.

say: For example, Amaka makes shea body butter. On 10 September she spends 91,200 naira on materials for 48 jars for a distributor.

panel.heading: How long is your cash tied up?
items: 10 September: 48 x 1,900 = 91,200 naira out
25 September: delivered, 15 days later
Net 30: paid 30 days after delivery
Cash cycle: 15 + 30 = 45 days

say: She makes and labels the jars, and delivers on 25 September.

say: The terms are net 30, which means payment 30 days after delivery.

say: So her cash cycle is 45 days. If the distributor pays 10 days late, it is 55. Before adding a second distributor, she checks she has enough cash for both cycles at once.

say: In a shop far away, you cannot see a bad jar before a customer does. So, habit one: print a batch code on every jar, and keep a record of where each unit went.

cards.d: Code every batch, like SB-2409-02, and record where every unit went.
Older jars to the front, new ones behind. Supply little and often.
Every 2 to 4 weeks: visible, priced right, not damaged or past date, rotated.

say: Habit two: first expired, first out. Shop staff often put new cartons in front, so rotate the stock yourself on every visit.

say: Habit three: a shelf check every 2 to 4 weeks, using the same questions each time. The units left also show your sell-through.

say: A channel can bring big sales and still lose you money. So start from the shelf price and walk backwards.

card.title: Walk back from the shelf price

say: The retailer keeps 30% of 4,000, which is 1,200, so it pays 2,800. That 30% is a margin, a share of the selling price. A markup is added to cost. Always ask which one a partner means.

card.title: Walk back from the shelf price

say: The distributor keeps 280 of that 2,800, and pays Amaka 2,520.

card.title: Walk back from the shelf price

say: Her cost is 1,900, so she keeps 620 naira per jar.

card.title: Walk back from the shelf price

say: After fees, delivery, ads and commission, direct and agent sales leave the most per jar, and the distributor the least.

panel.heading: Profit per jar or profit per month

say: But the distributor might move 300 jars a month, for 186,000 naira, with no ads and no chatting. Direct sales stuck at 100 orders give 164,000. So compare total monthly profit, your time and your capacity.

panel.heading: Profit per jar or profit per month

say: To remember. Write a short routine for each channel, and keep one order and payment log that you check every week. Count your cash cycle. Code every batch and rotate stock. And judge each channel on its true monthly profit, not on sales alone.

panel.heading: Remember
items: A sale ends when the money is recorded
Write a one-page SOP for each channel
Count your cash cycle in days
Code batches, rotate stock, trace complaints
Judge channels on true monthly profit
